title: Assessment & Practical Test
subtitle: Ten weeks, done rather than written.
objectives: Recall the kitchen and safety weeks
Recall the food preparation and cooking weeks
Recall the clothing and sewing weeks
Plan and run the practical test

cards.title: Ten weeks, done rather than written
cards.text: The test asks you to do things. So revision here is readiness, not recall.

cards.title: Weeks 1 to 4
cards.text: The four that carry most of the marks.
points: **Tools:** right tool, thermometer over colour, sharp is safe.
**Zones:** store, wash, prep, cook. One direction.
**Safety:** 5 to 60°C, two hours total, no reset.
**Pantry:** FIFO, 4°C and -18°C, use by against best before.

cards.title: Ten weeks, what is marked
cards.text: Tap each week. The second line is the trap.

question.text: What is the temperature danger zone?

cards.title: Weeks 5 to 7
cards.text: Where the practical marks actually come from.
points: **Cuts:** equal beats fine; the claw grip.
**Measuring:** level dry, eye level for liquid.
**No-cook:** no kill step, so handling is everything.
**Heat:** water stops at 100°C, so nothing browns in it.

question.text: Why can nothing brown in boiling water?
options: Water cannot exceed 100°C; browning needs about 140°C
question.explain: A physical ceiling, not a technique problem.

cards.title: Weeks 8 to 10
cards.text: The three that get least practice and most lost marks.
points: **Labels:** five shapes, and a cross means do not.
**Stains:** cold water for protein; heat sets it.
**Stitches:** backstitch holds, basting comes out.
**System:** one home per object, fixed days.

cards.title: Rehearse the order, not the facts
cards.text: In a practical test you lose marks on sequence, not on knowledge.
points: **Wash hands. Set the station. Then touch food.**
**Say the step out loud** as you do it.
**Markers are watching the order**, not your speed.
**Do it slowly and correctly.**

cards.title: Know what is scored
cards.text: A practical has a rubric, and the rubric is not a secret.
points: **Hygiene. Safety. Sequence. Result. Clean-up.**
**Clean-up is marked** and is the one people skip.
**The result is one part of five.**
**Lose nothing on the parts that are free.**

question.text: Which part of a practical do people most often skip?

cards.title: This is what gets marked
cards.alt: Ingredients pre-measured into small bowls arranged in an arc beside a clean board, a knife and a cold pan
cards.text: Everything measured and in place before any heat. Markers watch the order, not your speed.

cards.title: Eat before, not during
cards.text: A two-hour practical on an empty stomach goes badly.
points: **Eat properly beforehand.**
**Water within reach**, away from the board.
**Tie hair back, sleeves up**, before you start.
**Those are marks too.**

cards.title: The five that matter
points: Hands and station before any food.
5 to 60°C, two hours total, no reset.
Equal cuts, levelled measures, the claw grip.
Clean-up is scored. Do not walk away from it.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 11 TLE, the practical. The deck is written as readiness rather than revision: what will be marked, which step gets forgotten, and the fact that clean-up is scored and is the part people walk away from. The review board names the trap for each of the ten weeks. The boxing lens gives the single most useful instruction for a practical exam (marks are lost on sequence, not knowledge, so say each step out loud as you do it) and the growth lens covers the physical preparation that also carries marks: hair tied, sleeves up, eaten beforehand. The twenty-four question paper is weighted towards the safety weeks, which is where the marks are.
discussion: Ask him to talk through a dish from washing hands to clean-up.
Ask what the five scored parts of a practical are.
Ask which week he feels least ready on.
Ask what he will do before the test starts.
extension: Run a full mock practical at home, timed, including clean-up.
Have him write his own rubric and mark himself against it.
misconceptions: "The result is what is scored." It is one part of five.
"Clean-up is after the test." It is part of the test.
